svg.title: Web basics: domain, DNS, IP address and HTTPS
svg.desc: A domain is the name in the link. DNS looks up its IP address. The browser then connects across the Internet over HTTPS to the website computer; DNS does not carry the page. HTTPS protects the browser connection and uses a certificate for the domain. The computer runs your application and returns a page or API response. Addresses are reserved examples.

svg.text: WEB BASICS · NAMES, ADDRESSES AND A SECURE CONNECTION
Carries the request and the reply
Runs your app and sends the page
Domain = the name · IP = the address · DNS = the lookup
HTTPS protects the browser connection. The lock is protection, not another computer.
